source_snapshot.title: fix(ingest): resolve tsconfig module mappings, with authority + security fixes
source_snapshot.body:
Carries **@Hiro-Chiba's #440** plus three review fixes, two of them security. Landing it here closes #440 as merged.

> ⚠️ **Merge with a merge commit, not squash** — contains Hiro-Chiba's two commits alongside mine.

## Their change (`7d83423`, `bf7a4b4`)

Resolves local TS/JS imports through `tsconfig.json`/`jsconfig.json` `paths`/`baseUrl` before the filename-stem fallback. New 360-line module. The follow-up commit fixes `$`-token expansion in wildcard substitution — **the CodeQL alert on #440 is stale** and can be dismissed after a re-scan (its multi-star rationale is unreachable: `matchPathPattern` rejects a second `*` before substitution).

## My fixes

**1. `795ec2c` — `baseUrl` claimed authority over every bare specifier.** `return config?.baseUrl ? [] : undefined` — but `[]` means *definitively not local*, and `baseUrl` matches every non-relative specifier. On any repo that sets it (the default in Next.js, CRA, Nest, most monorepo templates) every third-party import including `react` became an authoritative miss and its IMPORTS/CALLS edges were silently dropped. Authority now requires an *explicit* `paths` pattern; a bare `baseUrl` and a catch-all `"*"` rule return "no opinion". This **replaces their `treats an unresolved baseUrl module as authoritative` test** — that behaviour is the defect. Their explicit-`paths` authority test is untouched and still passes.

**2. `9e58df1` — three security holes on the config-reading path.** All reachable from repo content, and all *before* ingestion's size gate (the resolver is built at `ingest.ts:1049`, 51 lines ahead of the `MAX_FILE_BYTES` check):
- **No size cap.** A 64 MB JSONC file — which git packs to a ~95 KB repo — gives `FatalProcessOutOfMemory`, signal 6, uncatchable. main skips it as `tooLarge`, so this was the first pre-gate whole-file read and it bypassed an existing control.
- **Device nodes and FIFOs.** `openSync` follows symlinks, so a link committed in the repo pointing at `/dev/zero` read forever (**exit 134, core dumped**); a FIFO blocked the event loop. Both report size 0, so a size check alone doesn't help. Under MCP the in-process runner means `withTimeout` can never fire and the server wedges uncancellably.
- **No containment.** `resolveExtends` only checked `startsWith(".")`, which isn't containment — `resolve` clamps at `/`, so enough `..` segments name any absolute path.

Fixed by opening once and fstat-ing the same handle (no stat-then-read window — CodeQL `js/file-system-race`, the pattern `ingest.ts` already uses), rejecting non-regular files and anything over 1 MB, and filtering `extends` candidates to inside the workspace. No content ever escaped — `resolveCandidate` only consults an in-memory Map built from the caller's file list.

**3. `c43303e` — memoization.** 24.87 µs → 3.38 µs per call, ~7.4x. Note the trap: the obvious `dirname` key is **wrong**, because `resolveCandidate` also reads the source *extension* (a `.js` caller prefers `.js`); keying on the directory alone serves one caller's answer to another. There's a test that runs both orders.

## Verification

Every fix mutation-tested individually. ix-cli 944 passed, 1 skipped; `typecheck`, `lint` (0 errors), `knip` clean.

commits.message:
fix(ingest): don't let baseUrl claim authority over every bare specifier

The resolver returned [] — 'definitively not local', which makes
resolveEdges skip both the stem fallback and the Tier-3 guess — whenever a
config merely set baseUrl. baseUrl matches every non-relative specifier, so
in any repo that sets it (the default in Next.js, CRA, Nest and most monorepo
templates) every third-party import, react and zod included, became an
authoritative miss and its IMPORTS/CALLS edges were dropped. A catch-all
'*' paths rule had the same effect.

Authority now requires an explicit paths pattern to have matched. A bare
baseUrl, and a '*' rule that is baseUrl by another name, return undefined
('no opinion') so existing resolution continues unchanged.

Also: a matching-but-failing paths rule no longer short-circuits the baseUrl
lookup, matching how TypeScript itself orders the two.

This reverses the decision pinned by 'treats an unresolved baseUrl module as
authoritative'; that test is replaced. The PR's actual goal — an explicit
paths mapping suppressing an unrelated same-stem match — is unchanged and
still covered.

Separately, resolveExtends probed candidates with existsSync before handing
the path to a reader (CodeQL js/file-system-race, the pattern view.ts calls
out explicitly). It now returns all candidates and lets the caller read each;
readObject already reports an unreadable file as undefined. That also fixes a
real bug: the probe stopped at a directory named by extends and never tried
<dir>/tsconfig.json, silently dropping the parent's paths.

ix-cli: 940 passed, 1 skipped. typecheck, lint, knip clean.

perf(ingest): memoize module resolution

Resolution runs per bound relationship, and index.ts issues two full lookups
of the same (source, specifier, kind) triple for each one, so a repo with
paths/baseUrl pays the walk over and over.

Cache on the three things that actually change the answer: the source
directory (which config applies), the source extension (a .js caller prefers
.js over .ts), and the specifier and kind. Keying on the directory alone —
the obvious shortcut — would serve a .js caller's answer to a .ts caller in
the same folder and silently flip the preference order, so there is a test
that runs both orders and a repeat.

Measured on a synthetic 2000-file workspace, 1000 calls across 50 source
directories: 24.87us/call -> 3.38us/call, ~7.4x.

ix-cli: 941 passed, 1 skipped. typecheck, lint, knip clean.

fix(ingest): bound and confine tsconfig reads

Three holes on the config-reading path, all reachable from repo content
because tsconfig.json is repo content, and all reachable before ingestion's
own size gate — createTypeScriptModuleResolver is built at ingest.ts:1049,
51 lines ahead of the MAX_FILE_BYTES check.

1. No size cap. readObject read and parsed any tsconfig whole. A 64 MB JSONC
   file — which git packs down to a ~95 KB repo — gives
   FatalProcessOutOfMemory, signal 6, which the surrounding try/catch cannot
   catch. main skips that file as tooLarge, so this was the first pre-gate
   whole-file read and it bypassed an existing control.

2. Device nodes and FIFOs. openSync follows symlinks, so a link committed
   inside the repo pointing at /dev/zero read forever, and one pointing at a
   FIFO blocked the event loop. Both report size 0, so a size check alone
   does not help. Under MCP this is worse than a slow ingest: the in-process
   runner means withTimeout can never fire and the server wedges
   uncancellably.

3. No containment. resolveExtends only checked value.startsWith("."), which
   is not containment — nodePath.resolve clamps at the filesystem root, so
   enough .. segments name any absolute path from any depth. An ingested repo
   chose which files on the machine were read, and a config outside the
   workspace had its paths trusted.

Fixed by opening once and fstat-ing the same handle (no stat-then-read
window; the pattern ingest.ts already uses), rejecting anything that is not a
regular file or is over 1 MB, and filtering extends candidates to those
inside the workspace root.

No content ever escaped: resolveCandidate only consults an in-memory Map
built from the caller's file list, so an escaped read could not reach output.
This is availability plus unauthorized read, now closed.

3 tests, each mutation-tested. ix-cli: 944 passed, 1 skipped. typecheck,
lint, knip clean.

chore: use the \\x00 escape instead of a raw NUL byte

I used raw NUL separators in a lookup key. They are invisible in most editors
and diffs — they render as a space — so the CI guard is the only thing that
sees them, and it is there precisely because a raw NUL makes the file binary
to grep/ripgrep, which then silently skips it.

The escape is the same byte at runtime, so behaviour and tests are unchanged.

fix(ingest): open config files non-blocking, and don't half-load a dropped extends

Three fixes from a rescan of the previous security commit.

1. The FIFO guard could never fire. Opening a FIFO for reading blocks until a
   writer appears, so the isFile() check — which runs after the open — was
   never reached. My comment credited it with stopping "a FIFO (blocks the
   event loop forever)", a protection the code could not provide, and the
   passing /dev/zero test made that look verified: a character device opens
   fine, so it exercised a different path. A repo-committed symlink to any
   FIFO wedged `ix ingest` before the parsing phase even announces itself —
   no output, no timeout, no error. O_RDONLY|O_NONBLOCK makes the open
   return; the existing fstat/isFile guard then rejects it correctly.
   Undefined on Windows, where the bitwise-or degrades to a plain read and
   there is no FIFO to open this way.

2. Containment over-rejected a legitimate sibling. A bare startsWith("..")
   also matches a directory merely *named* with leading dots, so
   `..shared/tsconfig.json` inside the workspace read as an escape and was
   dropped silently. Compare path segments instead.

3. A dropped extends left a half-loaded config, which is worse than main. A
   scoped run (`ix map ./packages/web`) roots containment at the ingest path,
   so a monorepo's shared tsconfig.base.json one level up is correctly
   refused — but the remainder still carried the package's own `paths`,
   which then matched, failed against the missing baseUrl, and returned an
   *authoritative* empty. That suppresses the stem fallback and deletes an
   edge main resolves fine. Treat such a config as unusable, which is exactly
   main's behaviour.

knip.json: mkfifo added to ignoreBinaries for the new POSIX-gated test.

Each fix mutation-tested; removing O_NONBLOCK hangs the suite outright.
ix-cli: 947 passed, 1 skipped. typecheck, lint, knip and the NUL guard clean.

fix(ingest): check containment against the file actually opened

Containment was pure path arithmetic, which cannot see through a
symlinked directory: every segment of "./linked/tsconfig.json" is inside
the workspace even when `linked/` points elsewhere, so an ingested repo
could still choose a file outside the tree by shipping one link. The
lexical check stays — it is what stops `../` traversal from the config
text — and the resolved path is now checked as well.

The resolve happens while the handle is open and is confirmed to name the
same inode, so swapping the link between the open and the resolve cannot
smuggle an outside file in under an inside name.

The workspace root is resolved too. Comparing a resolved file against an
unresolved root rejects every config whenever the root is itself reached
through a link — macOS /var -> /private/var, a home on a network mount, a
~/code symlink — which would have switched tsconfig resolution off for
those users with no error. The matrix here is ubuntu + windows, so no
runner would have caught it; the added test uses a symlinked root.

comments.body:
Added one more commit (`adc97c1`) closing the symlink gap I flagged as non-blocking earlier.

Containment was pure path arithmetic, which cannot see through a symlinked directory: every segment of `./linked/tsconfig.json` is inside the workspace even when `linked/` points elsewhere, so an ingested repo could still name a file outside the tree by shipping one link. Wrote the failing test first to confirm the escape was real rather than theoretical.

The lexical check stays — it is what stops `../` traversal from the config text — and the resolved path is now checked too. The resolve happens while the handle is open and is confirmed to name the same inode, so swapping the link between the open and the resolve cannot smuggle an outside file in under an inside name.

The part I would most like a second pair of eyes on: **the workspace root is resolved too.** Comparing a resolved file against an unresolved root rejects every config whenever the root is itself reached through a link — macOS `/var` -> `/private/var`, a home on a network mount, a `~/code` symlink. That would have switched tsconfig resolution off entirely for those users, with no error and nothing in CI to catch it, since the matrix here is ubuntu + windows. The added test uses a symlinked root specifically to hold that down.

Both halves mutation-tested: dropping the containment call fails only the escape test, and comparing against the unresolved root fails only the symlinked-root test. Full `test:unit` is 949 passing.

Context for the review: this is the same module where my earlier "fix" for FIFOs shipped a guard that could not fire (the non-regular-file check sat *after* an open that blocks forever on a FIFO), with a comment asserting it worked and a passing `/dev/zero` test that exercised a different path. That is why I am flagging the root-resolution decision explicitly rather than letting it ride on my own reading.

Found and independently verified an additional ingest correctness regression in the current #445 implementation: a configured module mapping names the module authoritatively, but the renamed-import fallback still binds `import { Base as LocalBase } from "@core"` to a class method `W.Base` — a member can never be a module export — emitting a confident wrong EXTENDS edge (@0.9) where the base never had one. The same happens for `import { type User as ExternalUser }`, which emits REFERENCES to `W.User`.

The issue is still reproducible against the current upstream PR state (head `adc97c1`), and I did not find an existing fix or duplicate PR addressing it.

Follow-up commit `f9274cc` applies the minimal fix — the same plain-key requirement on the configured-binding path — and adds regression coverage for the configured renamed EXTENDS and REFERENCES cases.

Verification: resolveEdges 72/72 on the fix tree, `tsc` clean; the wrong edges reproduce against `adc97c1` and are eliminated after.

Follow-up commit:
https://github.com/Alot1z/Ix-remap/commit/f9274cc0870c65a496a5b983c814d9fed6a65c0f

This is ready for the PR author/maintainer to review/cherry-pick.
